note: archon identity-floor conformance vectors. Every case here is stated entirely in RFC 8032 (Ed25519), RFC 5280 (SPKI) and RFC 5958 (PKCS#8) vocabulary: a seed, a public key, a signature, an opaque message, a key text, a PEM. No case needs the words root, admission, grant, fact, receipt or epoch to say what it means. That is the one-change-authority test, and it is why these four families live below the law rather than inside it. The first four families were copied from thesmos vectors/authority.json @ d878832 on 2026-08-22; thesmos deleted its copy at the switch (2026-08-27, thesmos) and drives its retained cases through archon. The hex_decode, domain_sign and domain_verify families are archon-authored (2026-09-09, docs/growth-plan.md).

pubkey_from_seed.note: the seed used by the signing_bytes/signature fixtures.
pubkey_from_seed.name: seed-11

pubkey_from_seed.note: the root seed used throughout the authorize family.
pubkey_from_seed.name: seed-22

key_encode.note: the canonical key text for the seed-11 public key (pubkey_from_seed/seed-11) — ed25519:<lowercase-hex>. Fixed format, hand-authored from the spec.
key_encode.name: seed-11-pubkey

key_encode.note: an all-aa 32-byte pubkey — encode is a pure prefix+lowercase-hex, so any byte slice round-trips (the bytes need not be a derived key).
key_encode.name: all-aa

key_encode.note: the all-zero 32-byte pubkey — the minimal encoding shape.
key_encode.name: all-zero

keycodec.note: the ed25519-key-codec-v1 PKCS#8/SPKI PEM codec (spec Appendix A.8). Each case names a `kind` selecting one of the four conversions; encode_* carries a raw-32 `key` (hex) and expects {"ok":"<PEM>"}, decode_* carries a `pem` and expects {"ok":"<raw-32 hex>"} or {"error":true}. Authored from the fixed DER templates in A.8 via an independent base64, NOT pasted from a core; confirmed identical on all three cores before pinning. The pubkey input is arbitrary 32 bytes (abab…) — the codec is byte-agnostic about key content. PKCS#8 is v1-only; v2 and bare DER are rejected.
keycodec.name: encode-pkcs8-v1

keycodec.note: encode rejects a key that is not exactly 32 bytes (here 31).
keycodec.name: encode-pkcs8-wrong-length

keycodec.note: CRLF line endings are tolerated on decode (the same key as decode-pkcs8-v1).
keycodec.name: decode-pkcs8-crlf

keycodec.note: PKCS#8 v2 (version 1 + embedded [1] public key) is rejected — v1-only (spec A.8).
keycodec.name: decode-pkcs8-v2-rejected

keycodec.note: non-zero BIT STRING unused-bits octet (0xff instead of 0x00) — rejected.
keycodec.name: decode-spki-bad-unused-bits

keycodec.note: trailing byte after the 48-byte template — rejected.
keycodec.name: decode-pkcs8-trailing-garbage

keycodec.note: bare DER with no PEM armor — rejected (decode is PEM-only).
keycodec.name: decode-spki-bare-der

keycodec.note: invalid base64 in the PEM body — rejected.
keycodec.name: decode-spki-bad-base64

keycodec.note: cross-template: a valid SPKI (PUBLIC KEY) PEM handed to the PKCS#8 decoder — rejected on the header label.
keycodec.name: decode-pkcs8-from-spki

keycodec.note: cross-template: a valid PKCS#8 (PRIVATE KEY) PEM handed to the SPKI decoder — rejected.
keycodec.name: decode-spki-from-pkcs8

signature_verify.note: Ed25519 VERIFY edge-cases (issue #52), distinct from the `signature` (sign) family. Inputs {pubkey, message, sig} are raw hex; expected {valid: bool} is hand-authored AND confirmed to agree on the real Rust (ed25519-dalek), Go (crypto/ed25519), and TS (@noble/ed25519) libraries before pinning — only cases all three demonstrably accept/reject identically are here. A valid signature: seed-11 pubkey over message 'Hello' (48656c6c6f).
signature_verify.name: valid

signature_verify.note: a single-bit-flipped signature (low bit of byte 0): rejected.
signature_verify.name: bit-flipped-sig

signature_verify.note: a wrong-length signature (63 bytes, the valid sig truncated by one byte): rejected on the shape guard before any point math.
signature_verify.name: wrong-length-sig

signature_verify.note: a wrong-length public key (31 bytes, the valid key truncated by one byte): rejected on the shape guard (Go crypto/ed25519.Verify would panic on a mis-sized key, so the cores guard length to false).
signature_verify.name: wrong-length-pubkey

signature_verify.note: the valid signature against a DIFFERENT message (last byte of 'Hello' changed o->p): rejected.
signature_verify.name: wrong-message

signature_verify.note: a non-canonical S (the valid sig's S replaced by S+L, L the group order): rejected. Go stdlib and ed25519-dalek (both its non-strict verify and verify_strict) reject the non-reduced scalar identically, and @noble/ed25519 enforces S < L by default — so all three agree.
signature_verify.name: non-canonical-s

signature_verify.note: a SMALL-ORDER public key (an order-8 torsion point, one of the eight documented Ed25519 small-order point encodings) with sig R=A,S=0 over 'Hello': rejected. This is the cofactored-verification (ZIP-215) gap from issue #106 — ZIP-215 ACCEPTS such keys (S=0 makes the verification equation [8](S·B) = [8](R + h·A) collapse since R=A is order-8 and h·A is also torsion), whereas RFC 8032 verification (Go crypto/ed25519, ed25519-dalek v2, and @noble/ed25519 with {zip215:false}) REJECTS it. The TS core previously accepted it under @noble's default zip215:true, admitting Head/fact evidence the canonical Rust core rejects; this vector byte-pins the rejection so all three cores agree. Authored from a documented small-order point, not pasted from a core.
signature_verify.name: small-order-pubkey-order8

signature_verify.note: a SMALL-ORDER public key (an order-4 torsion point) with sig R=A,S=0 over 'Hello': rejected. Same ZIP-215-vs-RFC8032 divergence as small-order-pubkey-order8 (issue #106), a different torsion order to widen the guard. RFC 8032 verification across all three cores rejects it; this pins that.
signature_verify.name: small-order-pubkey-order4

signature_verify.note: a domain-separated signature (domain_sign/v1-hello, Ed25519ph with context) presented to RAW verify: rejected. Domain separation is cryptographic, not a byte convention — the same bytes under the same key are not a raw signature. Expected values derived with OpenSSL 3.2.4 (`pkeyutl -rawin -pkeyopt instance:Ed25519ph -pkeyopt context-string:<domain>`), an implementation outside all three cores, per vectors/README.md: a vector captured from a core pins that core's bugs; one derived independently lets all three be wrong together and be caught.
signature_verify.name: domain-sig-never-raw

hex_decode.note: typed fixed-size hex decoders (hexbytes): `kind` selects seed (32) | pubkey (32) | signature (64); the case carries `hex` and expects {"ok":"<lowercase hex of the decoded bytes>"} or {"error":true}. Either case is accepted on input; output is always lowercase. No 0x, no whitespace. The decision (accept/reject) must agree across cores; the reject reason is each core's own.
hex_decode.name: seed-lowercase

domain_sign.note: domain-separated signing: Ed25519ph (RFC 8032 §5.1) with the domain as the context string. Inputs {seed, domain, message}; expected {"ok":"<128-hex signature>"} or {"error":true}. A domain is 1..=255 bytes; the empty domain is rejected on purpose ("sign in no domain" is what this exists to make impossible). Expected values derived with OpenSSL 3.2.4 (`pkeyutl -rawin -pkeyopt instance:Ed25519ph -pkeyopt context-string:<domain>`), an implementation outside all three cores, per vectors/README.md: a vector captured from a core pins that core's bugs; one derived independently lets all three be wrong together and be caught.
domain_sign.name: v1-hello

domain_sign.note: same key, same message, different domain: a different signature.
domain_sign.name: v2-hello

domain_sign.note: 256 bytes exceeds the RFC 8032 context bound: refused.
domain_sign.name: domain-256-rejected

domain_verify.note: domain-separated verify: inputs {pubkey, domain, message, sig}, expected {valid: bool}. Total, like signature_verify: every shape failure — including an empty or over-long domain — is false. The cases that matter are the crossings: a signature from domain A in domain B, and a raw signature in any domain, are both false, cryptographically. Expected values derived with OpenSSL 3.2.4 (`pkeyutl -rawin -pkeyopt instance:Ed25519ph -pkeyopt context-string:<domain>`), an implementation outside all three cores, per vectors/README.md: a vector captured from a core pins that core's bugs; one derived independently lets all three be wrong together and be caught.
domain_verify.name: v1-in-v1

domain_verify.note: the v1 signature presented in domain v2: rejected.
domain_verify.name: v1-in-v2-rejected

domain_verify.note: the v2 signature in its own domain: accepted (both directions of the crossing are pinned).
domain_verify.name: v2-in-v2

domain_verify.note: a RAW Ed25519 signature over the same message under the same key, presented in a domain: rejected. Raw never crosses into a domain.
domain_verify.name: raw-never-in-domain

domain_verify.note: empty domain: always false, whatever the signature.
domain_verify.name: domain-empty-rejected

domain_verify.note: another message in the right domain: rejected.
domain_verify.name: other-message-rejected

domain_verify.note: bit-flipped signature (low bit of byte 0): rejected.
domain_verify.name: bit-flipped-sig

domain_verify.note: 31-byte public key: shape failure, false — never a panic.
domain_verify.name: pubkey-31-bytes
